#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd | --flag-test> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]
# The course's Assignment 6 wrapper, merged with this repository's by Claude Code (7 Nov 2026).
# From the course's, new in Assignment 6:
# - `realtime` in place of a frame rate runs without --fixed-fps, for tests that wait on audio
#   (timers follow game time and fire correctly at a fixed rate, but audio plays on the clock);
#   its log is <name>_realtime.log;
# - an optional third argument sets the timeout in seconds (120 by default), for the cost script.
# Kept from this repository's Assignment 5 wrapper:
# - the Godot project is the repository root, so --path . (the course's has --path godot);
# - Godot isn't on the PATH on the author's machine, so it is found from GODOT, then `godot`,
#   then the two places the .bat launchers look;
# - the earlier checks run inside the main scene from a flag (`-- --sound-test`), so an
#   argument that starts with -- runs main.tscn with that flag instead of a tests/ script.
# The exit status is 1 if the log has SHADER ERROR or SCRIPT ERROR, and 124 if the test hung.
set -o pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
godot="${GODOT:-$(command -v godot || true)}"
for g in ../Godot/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe "$LOCALAPPDATA/Programs/Godot/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"; do
	if [ -z "$godot" ] && [ -f "$g" ]; then godot="$g"; fi
done
if [ -z "$godot" ]; then echo "Godot not found: set GODOT to its executable"; exit 1; fi
mkdir -p logs
if [ "$2" = "realtime" ]; then
	fps_args=(); tag="realtime"
else
	fps_args=(--fixed-fps "$2"); tag="${2}fps"
fi
if [[ "$1" == --* ]]; then
	log="logs/${1#--}_${tag}.log"
	timeout "${3:-120}" "$godot" --headless --path . "${fps_args[@]}" -- "$1" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
else
	log="logs/$(basename "$1" .gd)_${tag}.log"
	timeout "${3:-120}" "$godot" --headless --path . --script "res://tests/$1" "${fps_args[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
fi
status=$?
if grep -qE "SHADER ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR" "$log"; then status=1; fi
exit $status

## Effect A, the leaf burst (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, "Effect A: leaf burst"): leaves burst out of
## the bush as he dives into it, and fewer as he hops out. Presentation only: it listens to
## the bush's `hiding_changed` (hide_spot.gd), reads where the bush is, and writes no game
## state; nothing in the game reads it. main.gd adds it beside the camp's bush (the brief's
## revision of 7 Nov 2026 allows that wiring).
## The retrigger rule is overlap: every event gets a fresh copy of the effect's scene, and
## a copy already playing is never touched, so a dive in and a hop straight out give two
## bursts alive at once (the brief's predicted failure 3 is a reused one-shot node).
## Each copy is freed on a timer once its longer emitter's lifetime, read from the copy,
## has passed, plus FREE_AFTER: a one-shot GPUParticles3D never emits `finished` on 4.7.2
## (CLAUDE.md, "Headless facts"). The timer pauses with the game and follows time_scale,
## as the particles do. Every setting is the scene's; this sets only where a copy stands,
## its amount_ratio for the hop-out, and emitting.
## Written by Claude Code on 7 Nov 2026.

const LeafBurst := preload("res://effects/leaf_burst.tscn")
## The hop-out's smaller burst (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, "The settings": "Hopping out").
const OUT_RATIO := 0.5
## How long past the longer emitter's lifetime a copy is kept before it's freed (seconds),
## as the preview does (previews/leaf_burst_preview.gd).
const FREE_AFTER := 0.1

## The hiding spot it follows (campsite.gd `bush`). Set before it's added.
var bush: Node3D


func _ready() -> void:
	if bush:
		bush.hiding_changed.connect(_on_hiding_changed)


func _on_hiding_changed(inside: bool) -> void:
	var burst := LeafBurst.instantiate() as Node3D
	add_child(burst)
	burst.global_position = bush.global_position
	var longest := 0.0
	for p: GPUParticles3D in burst.get_children():
		if not inside:
			p.amount_ratio = OUT_RATIO
		p.emitting = true
		longest = maxf(longest, p.lifetime)
	get_tree().create_timer(longest + FREE_AFTER, false).timeout.connect(burst.queue_free)
extends Node3D
## Effect B, the campfire smoke (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, "Revised 8 Nov 2026: Effect B, the campfire
## smoke", and "Effect B's wiring, for Step 3"): one copy of effects/campfire_smoke.tscn at
## the fire pit, driven by the fire's `strength` (camp_fire.gd). Presentation only: it reads
## `strength` and `burning()`, writes nothing but its own copy, and nothing in the game reads
## it. main.gd adds it after the developer start points have set the fire.
##   - The feedback: every frame, amount_ratio = strength (0 out, 0.3 a log, 1 at full).
##     `amount` and every other setting are the scene's and are never touched (the brief's
##     predicted failure 4 is a loop that changes `amount`).
##   - Start and stop: emitting = burning(). Turned off, no new puffs come; those already in
##     the air should rise away and finish (a headless run can't show it: the strip does).
##   - The copy's state is set before it enters the tree, so the scene's 3.5 s preprocess
##     builds a column only over a burning fire, and none over a cold one.
##   - Paused, it doesn't process (it inherits the tree's pause), so nothing changes; hidden,
##     it keeps following `strength`, so there's no jump when it's shown again.
## Written by Claude Code on 8 Nov 2026.

const CampfireSmoke := preload("res://effects/campfire_smoke.tscn")

## The fire it follows (campsite.gd `campfire`). Set before it's added.
var fire: Node3D
## The copy's root (moved and hidden as a whole), and its one emitter.
var root: Node3D
var smoke: GPUParticles3D


func _ready() -> void:
	root = CampfireSmoke.instantiate() as Node3D
	smoke = root.get_node("Smoke") as GPUParticles3D
	_follow()
	add_child(root)
	root.global_position = fire.global_position


func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	_follow()


func _follow() -> void:
	smoke.amount_ratio = fire.strength
	var burning: bool = fire.burning()
	if smoke.emitting != burning:
		smoke.emitting = burning

extends Node3D
## Builds the forest, the props, the raccoon and the to-do list. The game opens on the
## title screen (title_screen.gd), shown over this level: him curled up asleep in his
## hollow at night with the lullaby playing. New Game glides the camera in to the nap
## close-up, and play starts from there when a move key wakes him. Any `--` argument
## other than the title's own (`--title-...`) skips the title, for the debug flags below.
## Debug: `-- --screenshot=out.png [--closeup] [--pose=<state> [--left]]` saves a
## frame and quits; --pose shows the raccoon in one state: an animation of the rigged
## model (idle, walk, run, sneak, bored, sleep, climb), or with USE_SPRITES a
## cut-out (see raccoon_sprite.gd). `-- --sprites` uses the cut-outs for one run.
## `-- --sound-test` runs the automated sound check (scripts/sound_test.gd).
## Screenshot helpers: --grab-test, --climb-test, --rest-test (he naps in the hollow),
## --tick-test (the bin is knocked over), --jump-test (he jumps on frame 1, F held; he's
## at the top around frame 14), --shot-frame=N (default 45), and
## --see-collision (the raccoon half see-through, for use with --debug-collisions).
## `-- --bubble-demo` adds a yard of stand-ins for trying the thought bubbles
## (scripts/bubble_demo.gd); `-- --bubble-test` runs their automated check in it
## (scripts/bubble_test.gd), with `--bubble-shots=<folder>` for a picture of each.
## `-- --camp-test` runs the automated check of the campers' reactions to the raccoon
## at the campsite (scripts/camp_test.gd), with `--camp-shots=<folder>` for pictures.
## `-- --tasks-test` plays level 1's camp tasks and routines through and checks them
## (scripts/tasks_test.gd), with `--tasks-shots=<folder>` for pictures.
## `-- --waves-test` checks the party's sound waves (scripts/waves_test.gd), with
## `--waves-shots=<folder>` for pictures.
## `-- --plan-test` checks THE PLAN, the to-do list on Tab, and the scraps at the bottom
## (scripts/plan_test.gd), with `--plan-shots=<folder>` for pictures.
## `-- --tutorial-test` plays the tutorial at the camp through with its guide on
## (scripts/tutorial_test.gd), with `--tutorial-shots=<folder>` for pictures.
## `-- --cones-test` checks the tutorial at the camp and the campers' cones and search
## (scripts/cones_test.gd), with `--cones-shots=<folder>` for pictures. The other tests
## skip the tutorial: for them the camp's tasks are on the list and the cones on from
## the start. `-- --cone-shader-test` checks the cones' shader and what drives it
## (tests/cone_shader_test.gd, cone_driver.gd), through the tutorial as --cones-test.
## `-- --leaf-burst-test` checks when and where Effect A, the leaf burst, fires as he dives
## into the bush and out (tests/leaf_burst_state_test.gd), with the tutorial skipped.
## `-- --smoke-test` checks Effect B, the campfire smoke, following the fire from cold
## (tests/campfire_smoke_state_test.gd); `-- --smoke-load-test` with it burning at load.
## `-- --fire-test` checks the campfire's life in the open world: the keeper building it,
## the bucket tipped with E, the fire lit again, and being seen further standing in its
## light (scripts/fire_test.gd, camp_fire.gd).
## `-- --tent-test` checks Dismantle the tent: its four pegs pulled with E, the tent
## falling, and the camper pitching it again (scripts/tent_test.gd, camp_tent.gd).
## `-- --dev-start=<point>` starts at a point of the developer menu (F1, dev_menu.gd):
## den, camp, roast, free (the fire out) or fire (burning); F9 turns vsync off and on.

const LowPoly := preload("res://scripts/lowpoly.gd")
const Player := preload("res://scripts/player.gd")
const Forest := preload("res://scripts/forest.gd")
const CameraTuner := preload("res://scripts/camera_tuner.gd")
const RaccoonSprite := preload("res://scripts/raccoon_sprite.gd")
## Draw the raccoon with the author's generated cut-outs (the asset slice, 6 Oct)
## instead of the rigged 3D model.
const USE_SPRITES := false
## --pose names from the cut-outs, as the rigged model's animations.
const POSE_ANIMATIONS := {"asleep": "sleep"}
const SoundTest := preload("res://scripts/sound_test.gd")
## Pictures over his head that show what he notices, wants or feels.
const ThoughtBubbles := preload("res://scripts/thought_bubbles.gd")

			failed = true
			print("FAIL %s: %d sampled frames in the wrong state (first: %s)" % [c, _bad[c], _bad_why[c]])
		else:
			print("PASS %s: every sampled frame in its stated state" % c)

	quit(1 if failed else 0)

## The effects' headless CPU price (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, "Price predictions and budget" for
## Effect A and "Price" for Effect B), in the manner of the chapter's cost script
## (Example 09; there's no copy of it in this repository). At a fixed rate it measures the
## CPU time of each frame in four cases:
##   empty     an empty scene (one bare Node): the control, the script's own floor;
##   game      the game scene (main.tscn) with both effects off;
##   effect_a  the game scene with Effect A at the most bursts the brief says can be alive
##             at once: two, a dive in and a hop straight out (short answer 3);
##   effect_b  the game scene with Effect B in its heaviest state: strength 1, burning,
##             amount_ratio 1 (all 40 puffs).
## Each case runs ROUNDS times, each time in a fresh copy of the scene, warmed up WARMUP
## frames and then sampled for SAMPLES frames; the cases take turns in each round, so a
## drift in the machine falls on all of them alike. Per case it reports the mean and the
## spread (standard deviation, min and max over frames; min and max of the rounds' means).
##
## What's measured: the wall time from one frame's process_frame to the next, which is the
## whole main-loop iteration (physics, process, the dummy renderer); `--fixed-fps` makes
## game time follow frames, so every case runs the same game time per frame. Beside it,
## the engine's own monitors (Performance TIME_PROCESS + TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS).
##
## How the cases are set, without changing any game or effect file:
##   - main.tscn starts as the game opens with no arguments: under the title, the fire's
##     cycle off, so its strength stays 1 (CLAUDE.md). That's Effect B's heaviest state,
##     and steady.
##   - "Off" is this script freeing the effect's node from its own copy of the level right
##     after it's ready, before its first frame: the leaf burst's listener (leaf_bursts.gd)
##     and the smoke's driver (main.gd `campfire_smoke`, with its copy of the smoke).
##   - Effect A is triggered by emitting the bush's `hiding_changed` (hide_spot.gd), the
##     signal leaf_bursts.gd listens to; nothing else in the game connects to it, so no
##     game state changes. A dive in, then the hop out RETRIGGER frames later (the brief's
##     preview retrigger, 0.33 s), then again once both are freed; only frames with exactly
##     two bursts alive are sampled.
##   - Each sampled frame checks the case is in the state it claims (bursts alive and their
##     amount_ratio; the smoke's emitting, amount_ratio and amount; effects absent). Any
##     frame that isn't makes the run fail.
## A headless run uses a dummy renderer that runs no GPU particle process (CLAUDE.md,
## "Headless facts"): this prices the effects' CPU side only. GPU time is the Visual
## Profiler's.
## Run: bash scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300
## Written by Claude Code on 8 Nov 2026.

const LEVEL := "res://main.tscn"
const LeafBursts := preload("res://scripts/leaf_bursts.gd")
const CASES := ["empty", "game", "effect_a", "effect_b"]
const ROUNDS := 5
const WARMUP := 120
const SAMPLES := 300
## Frames between the dive-in burst and the hop-out burst (0.33 s at 60 fps).
const RETRIGGER := 20
## The hop-out's ratio (leaf_bursts.gd OUT_RATIO) and the smoke's amount (the brief).
const OUT_RATIO := 0.5
const SMOKE_AMOUNT := 40

## case -> every sampled frame's wall time (ms); the engine monitors' (ms); each round's mean.
var _wall := {}
var _engine := {}
var _round_means := {}
## case -> frames sampled in the wrong state, and the first such reason.
var _bad := {}
var _bad_why := {}
var _last := 0


func _initialize() -> void:
	for c: String in CASES:
		_wall[c] = []
		_engine[c] = []
		_round_means[c] = []
		_bad[c] = 0
		_bad_why[c] = ""
	_run()


func _run() -> void:
	print("Effects' headless CPU price (tests/cost_effects.gd)")
	print("  args: %s" % [OS.get_cmdline_args()])
	print("  renderer: %s, adapter: '%s'" % [RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_method(),
		RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_name()])
	print("  physics ticks/s: %d, max_fps: %d, rounds: %d, warm-up: %d frames, samples: %d frames a case a round"
		% [Engine.physics_ticks_per_second, Engine.max_fps, ROUNDS, WARMUP, SAMPLES])
	var t0 := Time.get_ticks_msec()
	for r in ROUNDS:
		# Rotate the order each round, so no case is always first or last.
		for i in CASES.size():
			var c: String = CASES[(i + r) % CASES.size()]
			await _measure(c, r)
		print("  round %d done (%.1f s)" % [r + 1, (Time.get_ticks_msec() - t0) / 1000.0])
	_report()


func _measure(c: String, r: int) -> void:
	var scene
	var bursts: Node = null
	var bush
	if c == "empty":
		scene = Node.new()
		scene.name = "Empty"
		root.add_child(scene)
	else:
		scene = (load(LEVEL) as PackedScene).instantiate()
		root.add_child(scene)
		for child in scene.get_children():
			if child.get_script() == LeafBursts:
				bursts = child
		bush = scene.campsite.bush
		if c in ["game", "effect_b"] and bursts:
			bursts.free()
			bursts = null
		if c in ["game", "effect_a"] and scene.campfire_smoke:
			scene.campfire_smoke.free()
			scene.campfire_smoke = null
	current_scene = scene
	for i in WARMUP:
		await process_frame

	var wall: Array = _wall[c]
	var engine: Array = _engine[c]
	var got := 0
	var sum := 0.0
	var since_in := -1
	var prev_alive := 0
	await process_frame
	_last = Time.get_ticks_usec()
	while got < SAMPLES:
		await process_frame
		var now := Time.get_ticks_usec()
		var ms := (now - _last) / 1000.0
		_last = now
		var eng := (Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_PROCESS)
			+ Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS)) * 1000.0
		var take := true
		if c == "effect_a":
			# Sample this frame only if it ran with exactly two bursts alive, at both ends.
			var alive := bursts.get_child_count()
			take = alive == 2 and prev_alive == 2
			prev_alive = alive
			if take:
				_check_bursts(bursts)
			# Then drive the next event: dive in when none are left, hop out RETRIGGER later.
			if since_in < 0 and alive == 0:
				bush.hiding_changed.emit(true)
				since_in = 0
			elif since_in >= 0:
				since_in += 1
				if since_in == RETRIGGER:
					bush.hiding_changed.emit(false)
					since_in = -1
		else:
			_check_state(c, scene, bursts)
		if take:
			wall.append(ms)
			engine.append(eng)
			sum += ms
			got += 1
	(_round_means[c] as Array).append(sum / got)
	if paused:
		_fail(c, "the tree was left paused")
	scene.queue_free()
	await process_frame
	await process_frame


func _check_bursts(bursts: Node) -> void:
	var ratios: Array = []
	for burst in bursts.get_children():
		var r: Array = []
		for p: GPUParticles3D in burst.get_children():
			r.append(p.amount_ratio)
		ratios.append(r)
	if ratios != [[1.0, 1.0], [OUT_RATIO, OUT_RATIO]]:
		_fail("effect_a", "burst ratios %s, not [[1, 1], [0.5, 0.5]]" % [ratios])


func _check_state(c: String, scene, bursts: Node) -> void:
	if c == "empty":
		if scene.get_child_count() != 0:
			_fail(c, "the empty scene has children")
		return
	if bursts != null:
		_fail(c, "the leaf burst's listener is still in")
	if c == "game":
		if scene.campfire_smoke != null:
			_fail(c, "the smoke's driver is still in")
		return
	# effect_b: the heaviest state.
	var smoke: GPUParticles3D = scene.campfire_smoke.smoke
	var fire = scene.campsite.campfire
	if not (smoke.emitting and smoke.amount_ratio == 1.0 and smoke.amount == SMOKE_AMOUNT
			and fire.strength == 1.0):
		_fail(c, "smoke emitting %s, amount_ratio %.3f, amount %d, strength %.3f"
			% [smoke.emitting, smoke.amount_ratio, smoke.amount, fire.strength])


func _fail(c: String, why: String) -> void:
	_bad[c] += 1
	if _bad_why[c] == "":
		_bad_why[c] = why


func _stats(a: Array) -> Dictionary:
	var n := a.size()
	var mean := 0.0
	for v: float in a:
		mean += v
	mean /= n
	var sq := 0.0
	for v: float in a:
		sq += (v - mean) * (v - mean)
	var sorted := a.duplicate()
	sorted.sort()
	return {"n": n, "mean": mean, "sd": sqrt(sq / maxi(n - 1, 1)), "min": sorted[0],
		"median": sorted[n / 2], "max": sorted[n - 1]}


func _report() -> void:
	print("")
	print("Per frame, wall time (ms), all rounds' samples together:")
	print("  %-9s %6s %8s %8s %8s %8s %8s   %-19s %s" % ["case", "frames", "mean", "sd", "min",
		"median", "max", "round means min-max", "engine proc+phys mean"])
	var s := {}
	for c: String in CASES:
		var w := _stats(_wall[c])
		var e := _stats(_engine[c])
		var rm: Array = (_round_means[c] as Array).duplicate()
		rm.sort()
		s[c] = {"w": w, "lo": rm[0], "hi": rm[rm.size() - 1]}
		print("  %-9s %6d %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f %8.3f   %8.3f - %-8.3f  %8.3f"
			% [c, w.n, w.mean, w.sd, w.min, w.median, w.max, rm[0], rm[rm.size() - 1], e.mean])
	print("  round means, in order: %s" % [CASES.map(func(c: String) -> String:
		return "%s %s" % [c, (_round_means[c] as Array).map(func(v: float) -> String: return "%.3f" % v)])])

	print("")
	print("Differences (the second case's mean minus the first's):")
	# Same within spread: the ranges of the rounds' means overlap.
	for pair: Array in [["empty", "game", true], ["game", "effect_a", false], ["game", "effect_b", false],
			["empty", "effect_a", true], ["empty", "effect_b", true]]:
		var a: Dictionary = s[pair[0]]
		var b: Dictionary = s[pair[1]]
		var d: float = b.w.mean - a.w.mean
		var same: bool = a.lo <= b.hi and b.lo <= a.hi
		var exact: bool = is_equal_approx(a.w.mean, b.w.mean)
		var line := "  %-8s -> %-8s %+8.3f ms (%+.1f%%)  %s" % [pair[0], pair[1], d, 100.0 * d / a.w.mean,
			"SAME within the spread (rounds' means overlap)" if same else "different (rounds' means don't overlap)"]
		if pair[2] and (same or exact):
			line += "  <-- should differ: the script may be measuring itself"
		elif not pair[2] and same:
			line += "  (the brief predicts this: no GPU particle process headless)"
		print(line)
	var limiter := absf(s["empty"].w.mean - 1000.0 / 60.0) < 0.05 * 1000.0 / 60.0
	if limiter:
		print("  <-- the empty scene's frame is about 1/60 s: frames are being paced, not measured")

	print("")
	var failed := false
	for c: String in CASES:
		if _bad[c] > 0:
			failed = true
			print("FAIL %s: %d sampled frames in the wrong state (first: %s)" % [c, _bad[c], _bad_why[c]])
		else:
			print("PASS %s: every sampled frame in its stated state" % c)
	print("Done: %s" % ("FAILED" if failed else "all cases measured in their stated states"))
	quit(1 if failed else 0)

The two effects cost nothing measurable on the CPU in a headless run, as the brief predicted. Nothing is committed, and no effect or gameplay file was changed.

## How it measures
- **What counts as CPU time:** the wall time of each whole frame (physics, scripts and the headless renderer). Each case gets a fresh copy of the scene, runs 120 frames to settle, then samples 300 frames. That repeats for 5 rounds, with the order of the cases rotated each round.

- **Effect A at its peak:** two bursts alive at once, a dive in and a hop out 0.33 s later. The script triggers them by sending the bush's `hiding_changed` signal. Only the leaf burst listens to it, so no game state changes. It only counts frames that ran with exactly two bursts alive, the second at `amount_ratio` 0.5.
- **Effect B at its heaviest:** the fire at full strength, smoke `amount_ratio` 1, all 40 puffs. `main.tscn` opens on the title screen with the fire's cycle off, so the fire stays at 1 for the whole run.
